metadata.name: peard
metadata.description: PEARD ASSETS: the registry of underlyings, and the ledger that pays holders in one

instructions.name: claim
docs: Claim units, settled in USDC at the current print.
`units` of 0 claims everything owed. The payout is scaled by
[`Market::coverage`], which is capped at 1.00: a rich vault pays face
value and banks the surplus for the next holder claiming into a dear
print. A haircut burns the full units - the difference is what lifts
coverage back up for everyone else.

accounts.name: quote_mint
docs: The quote mint itself, which Token-2022 makes mandatory rather than
optional: `transfer_checked` verifies the decimals against it, and
the associated-token address depends on which token program issued
it, so neither can be inferred from the market alone.

instructions.name: convert_inbox
docs: Turn a Native market's dollar inbox into the asset its vault holds.
A pool pays fees in its own quote token, and no venue will quote a
bonding curve in shares of Apple, so a market whose vault holds the
real asset receives dollars it has nothing to do with. This closes
that gap, and it is deliberately not a swap: the program has no
route, no venue, and no CPI into one. It posts a standing offer
instead - deliver the asset at the oracle price less a bounty, take
the dollars - and lets anyone holding a quote decide whether that
offer is worth filling.
The oracle appears here and still nowhere in a trading path, and
refusing to convert costs nothing: on a stale or frozen price the
dollars simply wait in the inbox until there is a price worth
converting at. Nothing is credited here either. The vault grows, and
`sweep_fees` sees it grow and credits it exactly as it credits every
other arrival, which keeps the protocol cut and the accumulator step
on one path rather than two.

accounts.name: quote_mint
docs: The quote mint itself, which Token-2022 makes mandatory rather than
optional: `transfer_checked` verifies the decimals against it, and
the associated-token address depends on which token program issued
it, so neither can be inferred from the market alone.

accounts.name: inbox
docs: Where the venue pays. Distinct from the reward vault by construction:
this is the market's dollar account, and a Native market's vault is
its asset account.

accounts.name: usd_token_program
docs: Separate from `token_program` on purpose. The dollar leg and the asset
leg are routinely on different token programs - USDC is classic SPL
and the assets this exists for are not - and assuming one program for
both is how a conversion silently addresses the wrong account.

instructions.name: create_market
docs: Attach a launched token to a pairable.
Permissionless, and deliberately incurious about the token: the mint
is already live somewhere, this only decides what its numbers are
counted in and where its fees settle.

accounts.name: creator
docs: Must be the token mint's own mint authority, while it has one.
The market PDA is seeded on the mint alone and there is no
`close_market`, so whoever calls this first owns that mint's fee route
permanently and the real issuer can never list. Nothing here checked
any relationship between the caller and the mint.
A renounced mint (authority `None`) stays open to anybody, which is
the honest reading: there is no issuer left to squat on.

instructions.name: deposit_fees
docs: Route trading fees in, and denominate them.
This is the step the whole design turns on. USDC arrives; the holder
ledger is credited in *units* at the current TWAP. The vault holds
dollars, the ledger counts bottles, and that gap is the exposure.
Permissionless because it only ever moves value inward: the fee
sweeper, the creator, or a stranger topping up the vault all take the
same path.

accounts.name: quote_mint
docs: The quote mint itself, which Token-2022 makes mandatory rather than
optional: `transfer_checked` verifies the decimals against it, and
the associated-token address depends on which token program issued
it, so neither can be inferred from the market alone.

instructions.name: expire_fulfillment
docs: Reclaim an open request the agent never settled.
Permissionless once the TTL has elapsed, because the alternative is
that a silent agent holds a holder's units, the vault's reserved
dollars and a slice of the epoch budget indefinitely. Identical
bookkeeping to a refund; the only difference is who may call it and
when.

instructions.name: open_position
docs: Open a reward ledger for a holder. One per (market, owner), forever.

instructions.name: push_price
docs: Push a price, USD e6 per one unit.
The relayer has already medianed its providers and applied its own
deviation gates; what happens here is the standing on-chain defence.
A push while frozen is refused outright, so a compromised oracle
cannot walk the TWAP breaker-step by breaker-step during a freeze and
hand governance a poisoned price at unfreeze.

instructions.name: register_pairable
docs: Register a thing with a number.
Admin-gated in v1 by design: the seed list is the marketing, and the
risk badge has to mean something before registration opens up. The
permissionless path arrives with the optimistic resolver, at which
point this instruction gains a bond rather than changing shape.

instructions.name: regrade_pairable
docs: Move a pairable between INDEX and HARD after it is registered.
The hole this fills: `grade` and `asset_mint` were written once by
`register_pairable` and reachable by nothing afterwards.
`update_pairable` covers params, provider count and fulfilment only,
and the PDA is seeded `[b"pairable", id]`, so the account cannot be
re-created either. When an asset's market died the registry file could
record it and the chain never heard, which is what happened to SLV and
TESOURO on 2026-08-25: both went on advertising HARD grade and a live
`asset_mint` to every client that reads chain rather than the file.
Freezing is NOT the lever for this and must not be reached for.
`frozen` means the price breaker tripped, and it stops accrual, claims
and fulfilment on every market the pairable carries. The problem here
is the asset's LIQUIDITY, not its price. The number is fine and still
worth settling against; it is the venue that emptied. Freezing would
say something untrue and charge live holders for it.
The two directions are not symmetric and the safety of this
instruction is entirely in the asymmetry.
**DEMOTION, hard to index, is allowed with markets live.** It only
narrows: afterwards `create_market` refuses Native here, which is the
whole intent. It cannot reach a market that already exists, because a
`Market` carries its own `quote_mint` and `quote_mode` and this
instruction writes neither. `grade` and `asset_mint` are read in
exactly one place in this program, the `QuoteMode::Native` arm of
`create_market`, and on no value-moving path at all: accrual, claims,
conversion, fulfilment and the roll all read the market's own copy.
Gating demotion on "no market exists" would be precisely backwards,
because the demotions that matter are the ones where somebody is
already exposed, and refusing those leaves the registry permanently
unable to say that an asset went illiquid.
**PROMOTION, index to hard, requires that no market has ever been
created on this pairable.** It widens: it makes Native markets
creatable against a mint this program has never validated and here
cannot, since the hard-tier mints are mainnet addresses that are not
accounts on the cluster the registry is seeded on. Vetting stays off
chain and by measured depth, exactly as at registration. Promotion is
also the only route by which a pairable's asset identity could ever
change: a repoint in place is refused below, but demote-then-promote
would walk around that in two transactions. `market_count == 0` closes
both at once.
That count is a high-water mark, not a live tally. It only ever
increments and there is no `close_market`, so it cannot tell a dead
market from an open one and a pairable that has ever carried one is
never promotable again. That is the conservative side of the error and
it is chosen deliberately: an over-strict refusal leaves the narrower,
truthful badge standing, while an over-permissive promotion hands a
live market a new asset.
`market_count` counts THIS program's markets and nothing else, which
is the right set rather than a convenient one. A peard_perps market or a
peard_tote round written on the same pairable reads the price index; neither
reads `grade` or `asset_mint`, so neither can be misled by a regrade.

instructions.name: request_fulfillment
docs: Burn accrued units and ask for the physical thing instead.
No coverage haircut applies: this is a budgeted valve, so a request
either fits inside the epoch budget at face value or it is refused.
The USDC is reserved rather than moved, which keeps the refund path
from depending on the agent holding funds.
`commitment` is a hash of the shipping payload. No address ever
touches the chain; the agent proves it holds the preimage.

instructions.name: retire_market
docs: Point a market at the venue its fees come from.
Display and provenance only: the pool address is never read to settle
anything, so a creator naming the wrong one misleads a chart rather
than moving a lamport. Updatable because a DBC pool migrates to DAMM
v2 at its threshold and the address changes when it does.
Close a market that never touched value, and give the pairable back.
`create_market` bumps `pairable.market_count` unconditionally and
nothing has ever decremented it, so a single market, including one
created by a stranger before this instruction pinned the issuer,
vetoed that pairable's promotion to `Hard` for good.
The conditions are deliberately absolute rather than nearly so. A
market that has credited a single unit, holds a single cent, or has
one holder earning is somebody's position and is not the admin's to
close, whatever the balances happen to net to.

instructions.name: roll_market
docs: Move a market from an expired pairable onto its successor.
Permissionless: the roll is fully determined by the two pairables, so
there is nothing to decide and no reason to make holders wait on an
operator.
The redenomination is **value-neutral at the instant it happens**.
Units scale by `old_final / new_price`, so a holder owed $10 of the
old thing is owed $10 of the new one, and coverage is untouched
because `units * price` is invariant across the change:
owed_after = (units * old/new) * new = units * old = owed_before
What does change is what a unit *means* from here on, which is the
whole point of a roll and the thing a UI must say out loud rather
than bury. `RolledOver` carries both prices and the factor so the
discontinuity is on the record.

instructions.name: set_backing_program
docs: Pin which program's backing attestations this one will believe.
Governance-only and global. A market creator who could name this
would be naming who vouches for their own backing, which is the same
as writing their own coverage number.

instructions.name: set_convert_bounty
docs: Retune what a converter keeps for filling the inbox offer.
This is the one number that decides whether anybody bothers: too low
and a Native market's fees sit in dollars forever, too high and
holders pay for the privilege of being converted. It moves because
swap costs move.

instructions.name: set_market_backing
docs: Point a market at the reserve that says what backs it.
Admin rather than creator: this decides what the coverage figure
means, and a creator naming their own attestation account would be
marking their own homework. Setting it to default detaches the
reserve, which is the honest thing to do when one is wound down.

instructions.name: set_terminal
docs: Name (or rename) the successor a dated pairable rolls onto.
Separate from registration because next year's crop has no price
today: `PEAR-CY26` has to be registered and trading long before
`PEAR-CY27` is a thing anyone can quote.
Move `terminal` and `successor` together, which is the only safe way.
They are a biconditional and nothing could set `terminal` at all, so a
chain that was registered rolling could never be terminated. That is
not hypothetical: the apple strip was seeded rolling from MAY into
OCTOBER, across the crop year, and no instruction in this program
could undo it.
WHY A CHAIN HAS TO BE TERMINABLE. For a perishable the strip is not
one continuous curve. Apples harvested in the autumn are stored
through the spring and then they are gone; the October contract is NEW
CROP and the May contract is old, and old-crop fruit is not
deliverable against a new-crop contract. Exchanges enforce this by
blacking out registration over the summer and force-cancelling
receipts before it. A roll across that boundary promises delivery of
something that will not exist, so the honest end of a storage season
is settle and redeem rather than roll.
Only while the pairable is still live. Past expiry the terminal has
already decided what happens to every market on it, and changing it
then would rewrite an outcome holders are already entitled to.

instructions.name: set_usd_mint
docs: Rotate the mint a Denominated market must quote in.
Governance-only and deliberately separate from `set_authorities`: it
does not change who is in charge, it changes what a dollar is. Live
markets keep their own `quote_mint`, so this only affects markets
created after it.

instructions.name: settle_fulfillment
docs: Report a shipment outcome.
Shipped releases the reserved USDC to the agent. Refunded returns the
units to the holder's ledger and gives the epoch budget back, so a
failed order costs the holder nothing and does not quietly consume
someone else's slot.

accounts.name: quote_mint
docs: The quote mint itself, which Token-2022 makes mandatory rather than
optional: `transfer_checked` verifies the decimals against it, and
the associated-token address depends on which token program issued
it, so neither can be inferred from the market alone.

accounts.name: position
docs: Credited back on a refund. Always the request's own owner.

instructions.name: sweep_fees
docs: Credit quote tokens that arrived in the vault by any route.
`deposit_fees` needs a payer willing to push; this pulls whatever
turned up. That is the whole venue integration: a bonding-curve fee
claim, an AMM sweep, a treasury top-up and a stray transfer all land
in the same account, and this credits the difference between what is
there and what has been accounted for.
Meteora's DBC sets a `fee_claimer` and collects in the quote token
only (`collect_fee_mode: 0`), so a claim deposits exactly the asset
this vault already holds - no swap, and no reason for this program to
know what a bonding curve is. The crank bundles the venue's own claim
instruction ahead of this one in the same transaction.
Permissionless, because it can only move value toward holders.

accounts.name: quote_mint
docs: The quote mint itself, which Token-2022 makes mandatory rather than
optional: `transfer_checked` verifies the decimals against it, and
the associated-token address depends on which token program issued
it, so neither can be inferred from the market alone.

accounts.name: token_program
docs: Named even though nothing here transfers: the associated-token
address depends on which token program issued the mint, so the vault
cannot be derived without it.

instructions.name: sync_backing
docs: Copy the reserve's published figure onto the market.
Permissionless, and it reads a foreign account by hand rather than by
CPI: the reserve program is pinned by governance, the address is
pinned by the market, and the bytes carry a magic and a version so a
wrong or moved account fails loudly instead of parsing into something
plausible. Nothing is trusted except the two pins and those constants.
The attestation carries its own `as_of`, and this stores it rather
than stamping the sync. A reserve nobody has marked in a week should
look a week old however recently somebody cranked this.

accounts.name: backing
docs: pins and its own magic. Never deserialised by Anchor, because Anchor
would need the type and that is the dependency being avoided.

instructions.name: sync_position
docs: Accrue what is owed and re-read the holder's balance.
Permissionless, and the asymmetry is the point. A holder's earning
balance only *rises* here, so buying more earns nothing until you
sync; but every accrual clamps against the live token account, so
selling stops earning immediately whether or not anyone cranks you.
Both directions favour the vault, and the leftover lands in
`pending_units_undistributed` rather than vanishing.

accounts.name: owner_token
docs: The holder's own token account, read to clamp the earning balance.

accounts.name: owner
docs: Required only to RAISE the earning balance, omitted to lower it.
Optional rather than mandatory so the heal stays permissionless: a
stranger must always be able to crank a seller out of the divisor,
and that is the direction that costs nobody anything.

instructions.name: withdraw_protocol_fees
docs: Sweep the protocol's cut. Permissionless: the destination is fixed by
`global.fee_receiver`, so there is no discretion to guard.

accounts.name: quote_mint
docs: The quote mint itself, which Token-2022 makes mandatory rather than
optional: `transfer_checked` verifies the decimals against it, and
the associated-token address depends on which token program issued
it, so neither can be inferred from the market alone.

types.name: Delivery
docs: How the thing reaches the holder.
A Big Mac cannot be posted - it is a hot prepared item with a ten minute
quality life - and neither can a gallon of petrol. For those the honest
deliverable is a claim on the good rather than the good, which is a
different promise and wants a different ceiling, floor and TTL. Saying
which on chain keeps the UI from implying a parcel is coming.

types.name: FulfillmentConfig
docs: The burn-to-ship valve. A budget, not an obligation: it can only ever
spend from the reward vault's own USDC, and only up to `epoch_budget_usd`
per epoch, so a run on it degrades into a queue rather than a drain.

fields.name: epoch_budget_usd
docs: Spend ceiling per epoch, USD e6.

fields.name: max_request_usd
docs: Largest single request the valve will quote, USD e6. Bounds the blast
radius of a bad print on the fulfilment path specifically.

fields.name: min_request_usd
docs: Smallest request worth shipping, USD e6.
A ceiling alone is not enough. Produce moves by the carton and
shipping one pear costs several times the pear, so without a floor
every request is economically absurd and the agent eats the
difference on each one.

fields.name: request_ttl_secs
docs: How long the agent has before anyone may expire an open request.
Without this an unsettled request holds its reserved dollars and its
slice of the epoch budget hostage forever if the agent goes dark.
Perishables make it worse: "we will ship when they are in season" is
indistinguishable from never.

types.name: FulfillmentRequest
docs: A burn-to-ship request. The chain records the burn, the budget draw, and
a commitment to the shipping payload; an off-chain agent does the rest
and reports back.

fields.name: units
docs: Units-e9 burned from the owner's ledger.

fields.name: quoted_usd
docs: USD e6 charged against the epoch budget at request time.

fields.name: commitment
docs: Hash of the off-chain shipping payload. No address ever touches the
chain; the agent proves it holds the preimage.

fields.name: fulfillment_authority
docs: Signs shipment outcomes for the fulfilment valve.

fields.name: fee_receiver
docs: Where the protocol's cut of deposited fees is withdrawable to.

fields.name: usd_mint
docs: The one mint a Denominated market may quote in. Pinned rather than
assumed: "USDC" is a symbol anyone can mint, and a market quoted in a
lookalike would price correctly and pay out in confetti.

fields.name: backing_program
docs: The program whose backing attestations this one will read.
Pinned by governance rather than named per market, because a market
creator choosing which program vouches for their own backing is a
market creator writing their own coverage number.

fields.name: protocol_fee_bps
docs: Protocol cut of every fee deposit, bps. The rest goes to holders.

fields.name: convert_bounty_bps
docs: What a converter keeps for turning a Native market's USDC fee inbox
into the asset its vault holds, bps off the oracle price. One knob
for the whole protocol rather than one per market: a per-market
setting is a per-market way to get it wrong, and the number only has
to beat a swap fee.

types.name: Grade
docs: What the quote actually is, which fixes what a holder can be owed.

types.name: Market
docs: One launched token quoted against one pairable.
The market holds no opinion about where the token trades. There is no
AMM here and no oracle in any swap path: the pool is an ordinary
external USDC pool that has never heard of the pairable. Everything in
this account is denomination and settlement.

fields.name: quote_mint
docs: USDC. Named rather than assumed so devnet and mainnet differ by
config instead of by code.

fields.name: fee_bps
docs: The pool fee that gets routed here, bps. Informational: this program
never collects it, it only receives deposits.

fields.name: pool
docs: The venue whose fees land in this vault. Display and provenance only.

fields.name: backing
docs: The published attestation of what real things back this market.
Default means none, and none is a market backed by its vault alone.

fields.name: backing_value_usd
docs: Last synced attestation, USD e6, and when the reserve behind it was
last known to be complete. Cached so that every other instruction can
see it without carrying a foreign account around.

fields.name: backing_max_age_secs
docs: Past this, a synced figure stops counting. Backing only ever drifts
upward of the truth when nobody is marking it.

fields.name: quote_decimals
docs: Decimals of `quote_mint`. Cached because every accrual and claim
scales by it, and re-reading the mint on each would be a wasted
account per instruction.

fields.name: acc_units_per_token
docs: Cumulative units-e9 per token base unit, ACC_ONE scaled.

fields.name: total_earning_balance
docs: Sum of every position's `earning_balance`. The accumulator's divisor.

fields.name: units_outstanding
docs: Units-e9 accrued to positions and not yet claimed or shipped. Equals
the sum of every `Position.units_owed` exactly, which is what makes
the coverage ratio a real number rather than an estimate.

fields.name: roll_index
docs: Cumulative roll factor, ROLL_ONE scaled.
One number reprices every position, exactly as floorlaunch's
`funding_index` reprices every CDP: positions carry a snapshot and are
brought forward lazily on next touch, so a roll is O(1) rather than a
walk over every holder.

fields.name: pending_units_undistributed
docs: Units-e9 that arrived with no one earning, plus the truncation dust
from every accumulator step. Rolled into the next distribution rather
than written off, so nothing silently leaks out of the ledger.

fields.name: vault_usdc
docs: Mirror of the reward vault's USDC balance, tracked by field so a
direct transfer into the ATA cannot silently reprice coverage.

fields.name: fulfillment_reserved_usdc
docs: USDC inside the vault already earmarked for open fulfilment
requests. Excluded from coverage and from claims: a bottle that has
been promised is not buffer.

fields.name: remaining
docs: The pairable's remaining market count, which is what gates a regrade.

types.name: Pairable
docs: A thing with a number. The registry of these, not the launchpad, is the
durable asset here.

fields.name: id
docs: ASCII, right-padded with zeroes. Doubles as the PDA seed, so it is
the canonical name of the thing: `COKE-20OZ`, `XAU-OZT`, `EGGS-DOZ`.

fields.name: unit_label
docs: What one unit is called in the UI: `bottle`, `oz t`, `doz`.

fields.name: price_twap
docs: USD e6 per one unit, EMA-smoothed. This is the number everything
else in the program divides by.

fields.name: frozen
docs: Set by the breaker or by governance. Blocks pushes (so a frozen
price cannot be walked) and blocks accrual, claims, and fulfilment.

fields.name: provider_count
docs: How many independent sources the relayer is *configured* to median.
A claim about setup, and only as true as whoever registered it.

fields.name: last_source_count
docs: How many sources actually agreed on the most recent accepted push.
The configured count above is an assertion in a JSON file and drifts
from the code the moment anyone edits either. This one is written by
the program from what the relayer passed with the price, so the badge
stops being a promise and becomes a record. When it sits below
`provider_count`, sources are down and the UI can say so.

fields.name: last_dev_bps
docs: Deviation of the last accepted push from the TWAP, bps.

fields.name: expires_at
docs: Unix time this pairable stops taking pushes. 0 means perpetual.
Dated pairables are the ones whose *definition* runs out rather than
whose feed goes quiet: a futures contract month, a crop year, a
valuation "as of" a particular tender.

fields.name: successor
docs: The pairable that takes over at expiry. Set iff `terminal` is `Roll`.
Not required to exist yet at registration: next year's crop has no
price today, and `roll_market` is where it is checked for real.

fields.name: asset_mint
docs: The tokenized version of this thing, if a liquid one exists on chain.
`Pubkey::default()` means none, and the program holds the invariant
that HARD grade and a set asset mint imply each other - a grade badge
promising redemption is only issuable against a mint that exists.
Vetting is off chain and by *liquidity*, never by symbol: at the time
of writing there are a dozen mints called SPYx and only one of them
has two million dollars behind it.

fields.name: twap_window_secs
docs: Window for the price TWAP (EMA weighting), seconds.

fields.name: min_push_interval_secs
docs: Minimum seconds between oracle pushes.

fields.name: breaker_bps
docs: A push deviating from the TWAP by more than this freezes the pairable
instead of moving it.

fields.name: max_price_age_secs
docs: Price older than this blocks accrual, claims, and fulfilment. Never
blocks trading, because trading does not read this program.

fields.name: asset_mint
docs: The mint after the move: the new one on a promotion, and
`Pubkey::default()` on a demotion, which is what withdraws the claim.

fields.name: market_count
docs: Markets this program already carries on the pairable. Nonzero here
means a demotion landed under live markets, which is legal and worth
being able to find later.

types.name: PoolKind
docs: Which venue a market's fees come from, so a reader knows how to decode
the pool account. Never read to settle anything.

types.name: Position
docs: A holder's reward ledger.
`earning_balance` only rises when the owner syncs, and every accrual
clamps it against the live token account. So buying more earns nothing
until you sync, and selling stops earning immediately whether or not
anyone cranks you. The asymmetry is deliberate and always favours the
vault.

fields.name: units_owed
docs: Units-e9 owed to this holder, already accrued.

fields.name: roll_snapshot
docs: The market's `roll_index` when this position was last brought
forward. Any gap is applied to both `units_owed` and `acc_snapshot`.

types.name: QuoteMode
docs: What the reward vault actually holds, which decides whether settlement
consults a price at all.

types.name: Resolver
docs: How a pairable's number gets on chain. This is metadata rather than
dispatch: every resolver funnels into the same `push_price`, and the
difference lives in the relayer. What it changes on chain is the risk
badge and which defaults a pairable is allowed to carry.

types.name: Terminal
docs: What happens when a dated pairable reaches its expiry.
The governing rule for both: **expiry never breaks a market.** Pushes stop,
so the last TWAP becomes the final print by construction, and accrual,
claims, coverage and fulfilment all keep working against it. A settled
market simply degrades into a fixed-conversion dollar market wearing a
historical label. Nothing is stuck and nothing is lost.
